title: Surjective evaluation from the principal w-localization to a prime localization
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, let W be its finite-partition principal w-localization [def-weil-pbc-w-localization], and let x be a prime ideal of A. At each finite stage, project to the unique partition part containing x and map its principal localization canonically to A_x [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. These maps are compatible with refinement. Let rho_x: W -> A_x be their induced A-algebra map. Then rho_x is surjective. The map, its stage formula, and the two-part cut indices are explicit constructions, rather than choices from a mere existence assertion.

proof.text: For each index i of [def-weil-pbc-w-localization] and prime x, select the unique partition part containing x. Its denominator is outside x, so the localization universal property gives a canonical A-algebra map from that factor to A_x [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Compose with the coordinate projection to evaluate the whole stage.

Under refinement the selected child has the selected old part as parent. Both composites from the old principal localization to A_x agree on A, so uniqueness of localization maps proves compatibility. The colimit universal property defines evaluation rho_x: W -> A_x, with its explicit formula on every stage injection.

Given z=a/s in A_x, cut Spec A into the nonempty members of D(s), V(s), with denominator s on D(s) and 1 on its complement. This is an allowed index, including when one part is empty. Put a times the inverse of the selected denominator in every factor; its value at x is a/s because x belongs to D(s). The stage tuple therefore maps to z. Fraction representation and the inverse-denominator identity are Mathlib localization lemmas.
